name: Alsace

rules.yield_base: 80 hl/ha for white, 75 for rosé, 60 for red

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Riesling, Gewürztraminer, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
One of 51 named grand cru vineyards, each its own appellation. The wine must come from that vineyard, name it on the label and meet stricter rules than plain Alsace AOC.
Late harvest. The grapes need at least 244 g of sugar per liter of juice for Riesling and Muscat, and 270 g for Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris.
Made from grapes with noble rot. They need at least 276 g of sugar per liter of juice for Riesling and Muscat, and 306 g for Gewurztraminer and Pinot Gris.
keyfacts: The Vosges mountains shelter Alsace from rain and maritime influence, so the region is rather dry and sunny.
Vendange Tardive (VT) and Sélection de Grains Nobles (SGN) were codified as late harvest designations on 1 March 1984, and SGN means grapes affected by noble rot.
Minimum must weights are 244 g/L for Riesling VT and 276 g/L for Riesling SGN, and 270 g/L and 306 g/L for Pinot Gris and Gewürztraminer.
Alsace AOC wine must be bottled in the tall Vin du Rhin flute, or in a bottle of the same tall, cylindrical, long-necked shape.

notes: Most Alsace whites come from aromatic grapes, so many are aromatic, floral and spicy.
Riesling here is known for dry wines, and Gewürztraminer for highly aromatic ones.
Labels on Alsace whites must state the sugar level, except on Vendanges Tardives and Sélection de Grains Nobles.
Long, dry autumns let Pinot Gris hang late, often giving very powerful flavors.
Vendanges Tardives wines often show very exotic, candied fruit aromas with a fresh finish.

blurb.text: France's mostly white wine region, with Germanic influence, where most wines are labeled by grape variety. Riesling and Gewürztraminer lead plantings in the Haut-Rhin and Bas-Rhin, then Pinot Gris and Auxerrois. Its appellations are Alsace, Alsace Grand Cru and Crémant d'Alsace.
